title: The Bird That Can Hear the Hill Fall Apart
before: 一台水下麦克风，和一个学生每年夏天去数一次，哪一个的证据更硬？读完给个答案。
paras: The Bird That Can Hear the Hill Fall Apart

The mountain yellow-legged frog is about the size of a thumb and the color of wet rock. For most of the year it sits still at the edge of a high lake in the mountains of California, waiting for insects to drift too close. It is not a loud animal. But in the spring, males gather in shallow water and call, and the sound carries across the valley.

Scientists used to count these frogs by walking the water's edge with nets. It took years, and it was hard on the frogs. So a team at the University of California tried something else: they put microphones in the water and left them there.

A hydrophone is simply a microphone built to listen underwater. The team placed dozens of them in lakes and streams, some of them for two full seasons. Then they trained software to pick the frog's call out of everything else - wind, rain, the slap of a bear drinking, the whine of a distant boat.

What the software found was not a number of frogs. It was the number of calling males per night, in each place, for months on end. And that changed the questions the scientists could ask. A count tells you how many frogs were there on the day you showed up. A nightly number tells you when they started, when they stopped, and what happened in between.

Frogs call when it is warm and when there is water. In the mountains, both are changing. Snow thaws earlier than it did thirty years ago, and some small lakes now dry out by August. A listening station records the date the first call arrives every year, and that date becomes a number you can compare - one that no one has to be present for.

There is a cost to this method, and it is not small. You cannot recognize an individual frog by its voice. If ten males call, you know ten are calling, not ten are alive. And a microphone that fails in November leaves a hole in the record that no one can fill later.

Still, the record is longer than any person's attention. A graduate student can spend three summers on one valley. A hydrophone can spend five years there without getting tired, and it does not mind the cold.

The team's conclusion was quiet, and it was not about frogs in particular. Some things in nature are not hard to measure because they are rare. They are hard to measure because we keep showing up to look and then leaving again.
after: 一句话主旨：两句话以内。
圈 3 个词：最挡路的，或者看着眼熟但说不准的。点一下就是圈了。
三句复述：一句概括、一句细节、一句你的判断（同意不同意，为什么）。
note: 机关在最后两段转：作者先说这套方法的两个代价（认不出个体、设备一坏就有空档），再在第 7 段把尺度换掉——比较的不是谁更准，是谁能待得更久。最后一段的 rare 是坑：真正的原因不是「稀有」，是「我们总是来了又走」。
